child.example: Sample data: this is a made-up person. Five of the eight sinuses are drawn inflamed so you can see the difference with the later date.
child.summary: SAMPLE DATA, not a real person. A winter of repeated sinus infections at age 9. A scan showed five of the eight sinuses inflamed. Treated with antibiotics; the adenoids were removed the same year.
child.source: Fictional example. To show your own records, put them in poc/data/records.json.

2020.summary: SAMPLE DATA, not a real person. CT of the sinuses: all sinuses clear and full of air, drainage channels open on both sides.

unknown: This is sample data, so nothing here describes a real person.
A real childhood record often says only "inflamed": no fill level and no measurements. The view then shows a state, not a picture of the actual disease.
Whether the drainage channels were blocked in the first record. They are drawn pale and still for that date because the sample record doesn't describe them.
next: With your own records: the hospital that made a CT scan can give you a copy of the images (DICOM files).
Letters from an ear, nose and throat doctor usually hold the clearest summary of what a scan showed.

child.text: Sample: the left ethmoid cells, between the eyes, were inflamed and the right ones were clear. A record can say something different for each side.

child.text: Sample: no childhood record mentions them.
